messages:
francis: FYI i'm drafting a short guidance block for the audit-export doc about redaction options and examples for SOC2. want to surface a small SDK snippet (py + go) showing the export call with redaction_level and an example output row showing a pseudonymized user_id. will open PR later today.
akiko: thumbs. please be explicit that pseudonymization is a transformation we apply at export time and is reversible only if the customer keeps the mapping key; do not imply we 'anonymize' data.
marina: legal +1 to akiko. also please add: "Customers are responsible for exported file handling; Redwood does not manage customer retention of exported artifacts" somewhere nearby.
francis: noted. drafting language: "Export redaction options let you choose how sensitive fields are handled in export payloads. Options: none, pseudonymize, redact. Pseudonymize replaces values with reversible tokens; redact removes the value entirely." ok to keep short?
omar: looks good. small nit: call the param "redaction_level" (snake_case) so SDKs match current conventions.
francis: changing to redaction_level. adding sample python snippet:```python
from redwood import AuditClient
client = AuditClient(os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
resp = client.create_export({
    "type": "audit_log",
    "range": {"from": "2025-02-01", "to": "2025-02-28"},
    "export_ttl_days": 30,
    "redaction_level": "pseudonymize"
})
print(resp["export_id"])
```
akiko: can you also include a minimal example of the output record shape? that helps legal and docs readers.
francis: added example row in PR:```json
{
  "timestamp": "2025-02-10T14:23:01Z",
  "event": "model.infer",
  "user_id": "usr_7f4a3e2b",
  "user_id_pseudonymization_method": "token_map_v1",
  "details": {"model":"rw-large","tokens":42}
}
```
marina: good. please add a short sentence: "pseudonymization metadata (e.g., user_id_pseudonymization_method) indicates how values were transformed; keep mapping keys secure if you need re-identification."
francis: added that exact line. also included a go example because partners asked for it:```go
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
req := redwood.ExportRequest{
  Type: "audit_log",
  Range: redwood.DateRange{From: "2025-02-01", To: "2025-02-28"},
  ExportTTLDays: 30,
  RedactionLevel: "redact", // example of full redaction
}
resp, err := client.CreateExport(req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
fmt.Println(resp.ExportID)
```
akiko: for the go snippet, change comment to show pseudonymize as the option in at least one sample; helps readers compare.
francis: fixed. also inserted a short migration note: "Note: older clients used ttl_days and redact_mode; current API accepts both keys for backwards compatibility but prefer export_ttl_days and redaction_level."
omar: can we add an inline cross-link to the data-retention page and the security controls appendix? reviewers will want links.
francis: yes linked to /docs/data-retention and /docs/security-controls. added anchor to the security appendix for pseudonymization details.
docs-bot: link-check started for PR #1493 1 checks queued
marina: last legal nit: replace any instance of 'we pseudonymize' with 'the export process may pseudonymize' to avoid implying a continuous process.
francis: updated wording across the doc. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1493 - requesting review from @akiko and @marina.
akiko: reviewing now. small copy edit on the first paragraph (send in PR review).
docs-bot: link-check completed: 21/21 links OK
akiko: left a couple of tiny comments, otherwise LGTM.
marina: approved.
docs-bot: PR #1493 merged by omar at 2025-06-18T09:12:40Z
francis: thanks team! i'll follow up with a short changelog line for the SDKs and ping ch-team about the partner note.
